character_facts: The original warrior sees itself as governed by duty rather than feelings.
The original believes its defining essence is spiritual, not merely physical.
The duplicate understands itself as materially identical to the original and uses that claim as both argument and threat.
characters_present: An armored spacefaring warrior, likely the original combatant
A duplicate or mirrored copy of that warrior
continuity_links: This page continues an ongoing confrontation between a warrior and its mirrored or duplicated counterpart.
The line about not trying the 'mirror' trick again indicates the duplication tactic has already been used earlier in the scene.
dialogue_meaning: The duplicate frames itself as a true physical replica, not just an illusion.
It tries persuasion instead of pure attack, linking its survival to the original's own survival.
The original defines itself by duty and rejects emotional manipulation.
The conflict turns on a distinction between identical physical form and non-copyable inner essence.
The page resolves the argument by showing the copy disintegrating after the confrontation.
locations: Near a large blue planetary body
Beside or near a circular space structure or vehicle component
lore_facts: A being or effect in this setting can produce an exact physical duplicate of a person, including flesh, bones, and weapons.
The duplicate can speak, reason, and attempt psychological persuasion.
Within the page's logic, a perfect bodily copy is still considered incomplete because it lacks the original's soul or spirit.
The duplicate's existence appears unstable enough that it can dissolve after being overcome.
plot_events: An armored duplicate declares that it is a perfect physical copy of the other fighter, including body and weapons.
The duplicate argues that harming it would be equivalent to self-harm and asks the original to surrender.
The original refuses, saying it has only duty and intends to destroy the opponent.
The duplicate insists that the two are the same.
The original counters that the duplicate misunderstands the difference between body and soul or spirit.
Both figures fire or project energy at each other, creating a bright collision in space.
The duplicate begins dissolving after the clash.
The original declares that physical copying cannot reproduce its spirit and warns the enemy not to repeat the mirror trick.
uncertainties: The exact identity or names of the two armored figures are not stated on this page alone.
One speech balloon near the energy clash is small and stylized; the exact wording may be slightly uncertain, though the meaning is clear.
The nearby circular object is visible but its exact nature (ship, station part, or other structure) is not confirmed on this page.
visual_summary: Two armored figures in spacesuits confront each other in open space near a large planet or moon and a circular mechanical structure. One figure claims to be an exact duplicate rather than a reflection and urges surrender; the other rejects the appeal. The pair exchange energy attacks, producing a bright burst, after which the copy begins to dissolve. A tall side panel emphasizes the vast emptiness of space and one combatant descending alone.
